page: Microsoft Azure D64a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DAv4 family, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7452 processor operating at 3.35 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 1638 GB SSD, while dedicated GPU hardware is absent.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct tradeoff between single-core and multi-core execution. The single-core CPU performance under stress-ng is poor, falling into the bottom 10% of tested systems. However, the server demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, with its Geekbench multi-core score, PassMark CPU score, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression placing in the top 25%. Memory subsystem performance is highly competitive; the PassMark memory score ranks in the top 10%, and cached small-block read-only memory bandwidth is strong at 4168.16 GB/sec. Large-block uncached memory operations and Redis SET throughput remain in the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D64a_v4 offers a balanced resource density profile, combining high vCPU counts with a standard memory ratio and local SSD storage without the premium of specialized compute or memory-optimized hardware classes. This makes it a viable option for multi-threaded workloads that can leverage parallel processing to overcome lower single-core speeds. Recommended workloads include database operations, multi-threaded data decompression, image processing, and small-model LLM inference.
